Resolve the exact missing closure for a snapshot with the target
release's own apt, fetch it, generate a flat apt repository, write the
lock plan, sign the manifest and assemble the bundle — in one step.
Inputs may be apt package names, https:// URLs to .deb files, local
paths to .deb files, or any mix, given directly or via --list/--local-dir.

The target is named either by --snapshot, a capture of the real machine,
or by --base, a stock release for a machine that does not exist yet.
Exactly one is required. Prefer --snapshot: it proves the bundle is
complete for that machine, where a base only assumes it.

Usage:
  debark build [pkg...] [flags]

Flags:
      --acknowledge-redistribution   suppress the interactive redistribution prompt (warnings are still recorded)
      --approved-keys string         archive key fingerprints resolution must satisfy
      --arch string                  dpkg architecture the --base describes (default: this machine's)
      --backend string               auto, local or container (default: config backend, else auto)
      --base string                  stock release to assume instead of a snapshot: a builtin id such as ubuntu:26.04/desktop, or a path to a base definition file
      --digest stringToString        expected digest for a URL input, upgrading its provenance to user-digest (URL=SHA256); repeatable (default [])
      --embed-binary string          copy a debark binary into the bundle at bin/debark-linux-<arch>
  -h, --help                         help for build
      --image string                 override the container image for the container backend
      --interactive                  ask for anything not given on the command line, then print the equivalent command (a terminal is required)
      --list stringArray             packages.txt-style input list; repeatable
      --local-dir stringArray        directory of vendor .deb files, scanned (not recursively); repeatable
      --no-prune                     with --update, keep superseded files instead of pruning them
      --no-recommends                override the target's Install-Recommends and exclude recommended packages
      --no-sign                      write an unsigned bundle explicitly
      --out string                   write the bundle as a directory (default when neither --out nor --tar is given: ./bundle)
      --policy string                local policy file evaluated against the plan
      --sbom                         write sbom.cdx.json (CycloneDX)
      --sign string                  signing key: a private key file, gpg:<keyid>, or plugin:<name>
      --snapshot string              snapshot of the real target to resolve against (exactly one of --snapshot or --base)
      --tar string                   write the bundle as a <name>.debark.tar.zst archive
      --update                       refresh indexes, re-resolve, fetch newer versions, then prune superseded files
      --upgrades                     add a full-upgrade pass for packages already installed on the target

Global Flags:
      --config string        config file path (overrides XDG discovery)
      --json                 print the documented JSON object for this command instead of human text
      --json-events string   stream NDJSON evidence events to PATH, or "-" for stdout
      --no-color             disable coloured output (also honours NO_COLOR and TERM=dumb)
      --profile string       named config profile to apply
